title: Agency is Real

canonical_node.axiom: Some entities possess intrinsic causal power, agency requires selection among alternatives, and some agents can affect coherence through choice.
definitions: Agency: capacity for selection among alternatives, reason-responsive and self-determined.
Causal power: intrinsic ability to produce effects, irreducible to constant conjunction.
Will: selection among alternatives, requiring multiple possibilities, reason-responsiveness, and self-determination.
Moral capacity: ability to affect coherence (C) through choice, where positive C is moral and negative C is immoral.
Agent: an observer with causal power; moral agent: agent with moral alternatives; redeemable being: moral agent responsive to grace.
derivation: Epiphenomenalism self-refutes: belief in epiphenomenalism is a conscious state that affects behavior, so consciousness has causal power.
Hard determinism undermines rationality: if all conclusions are determined, they are not responsive to evidence, so no rational grounds for determinism.
Eliminativism self-refutes: denying mental states requires propositional attitudes, which are mental states.
Causal power is real: physics uses causal language; eliminating causation eliminates physics.
Will is real: deliberation assumes alternatives; quantum indeterminism provides physical indeterminism; freedom = indeterminism + reason-responsive selection.
Moral capacity is real: we hold people responsible; moral discourse is irreducible.
canonical_node.action: Treat agents as genuine causes; recognize that choices affect coherence; uphold moral responsibility; integrate agency with observation and divine partnership.
boundary: Does not claim to prove free will in a deterministic sense; only that agency is real and irreducible.
Does not specify the exact mechanism of quantum collapse or how agent selection works.
Does not claim all entities are agents; only some possess causal power and moral capacity.
Does not resolve the compatibility of divine sovereignty and human agency; only asserts they cooperate.
test: Check that the self-refutation arguments are logically valid.
Verify that the equations (e.g., C = f(choice)) are consistent with definitions.
Assess whether the defense grid responses adequately address common objections.
Confirm that the document does not overstate empirical evidence (e.g., Libet experiments).

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a framework for treating agents as causal entities with moral capacity, linking consciousness to causation and enabling theological integration.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the prior axiom that actualization requires an actualizer by identifying agents as the actualizers.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If agency is removed, the chain of actualization lacks a causal source, and moral responsibility becomes meaningless, undermining the entire framework.
dg5_translation_registers: Physics: causal power, quantum indeterminism, observer effect
Theology: imago Dei, divine command to choose, divine-human cooperation

overstatement_risks: Claims self-refutation of epiphenomenalism, determinism, and eliminativism without rigorous formal proof.
Uses quantum indeterminism as a necessary condition for freedom without establishing a causal link.
Asserts that evolution doesn't select for useless side effects, which is an oversimplification.
Treats universal moral practices as evidence for moral realism, which is a weak inference.
kill_conditions: If causal power is shown to be eliminable from physics without loss of explanatory power.
If a deterministic account of reason-responsiveness is provided that undermines the need for indeterminism.
If moral responsibility is convincingly shown to be a social construct with no objective basis.
risk.lean_target: Axiom 014: Causal power is real; Axiom 015: Will is real; Axiom 016: Moral capacity is real.

plain_summary: This document argues that agency is real, against epiphenomenalism, hard determinism, and eliminativism, using self-refutation arguments and philosophical reasoning. It defines agency as causal power with selection among alternatives and moral capacity. The document is philosophically coherent but lacks formal proof; it is best treated as a narrative anchor rather than a proven axiom.
